1	# Literature Incremental Scan: Model Collapse + Synthetic Text Detection (2025-2026)
2	
3	> Scan date: 2026-05-13
4	> Coverage: 2025-01 to 2026-05
5	> Purpose: Expand related work for gen-depth-contamination paper; assess novelty threats
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Novelty Impact Summary
10	
11	| Question | Answer | Impact on Our Paper |
12	|----------|--------|-------------------|
13	| Has anyone done **ordinal depth estimation** (K prediction, not binary)? | **No** | Core novelty intact |
14	| Has anyone quantified a **discrimination boundary K*** (saturation point)? | **No** | Core novelty intact |
15	| New detection features usable as baselines? | **Yes** — DivEye (surprisal diversity), MAGRET (contrastive rewriting) | Add as baselines in full study |
16	| New model collapse results that change our framing? | **Yes** — Schaeffer 2025 clarifies 8 definitions; need precise positioning | Tighten our definition of "collapse" vs "saturation" |
17	
18	---
19	
20	## Thread 1: Binary Synthetic Text Detection
21	
22	### [NEW] DivEye: Diversity Boosts AI-Generated Text Detection
23	- **Authors**: Basani, Chen (IBM Research)
24	- **Venue**: TMLR 2026 (also PAN 2025 shared task)
25	- **URL**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18880
26	- **Core contribution**: Zero-shot detector based on surprisal diversity — measures how token-level surprisal fluctuates across text. Human text has richer variability in lexical/structural unpredictability than LLM outputs. Outperforms existing zero-shot detectors by up to 33.2%.
27	- **Relation to us**: **Complementary / potential baseline**. DivEye features (surprisal diversity statistics) could be added to our feature set for depth estimation. The "rhythmic unpredictability" signal may degrade monotonically with generation depth — worth testing.
28	- **Code**: https://github.com/IBM/diveye
29	
30	### [NEW] MAGRET: Machine-generated Text Detection with Rewritten Texts
31	- **Authors**: Huang, Cao, Luo, Guan, Liu
32	- **Venue**: COLING 2025
33	- **URL**: ht
…[truncated 12862 chars]

tool_args.content:
papers:
  # === Must-Cite ===

  - id: drayson2025
    title: "Machine-generated text detection prevents language model collapse"
    authors: "Drayson, Yilmaz, Lampos"
    venue: "EMNLP 2025"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.15654"
    code: "https://github.com/GeorgeDrayson/model_collapse"
    category: "verification-curation"
    role: "direct-competitor"
    relevance: "Binary MGT detection + importance resampling for collapse prevention; our depth estimator generalizes their binary detector to ordinal depth"
    cited: false

  - id: schaeffer2025position
    title: "Position: Model Collapse Does Not Mean What You Think"
    authors: "Schaeffer, Kazdan, Koyejo et al."
    venue: "ICML 2025"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.03150"
    category: "model-collapse"
    role: "framing-critical"
    relevance: "Identifies 8 definitions of model collapse across 3 families; forces us to position K* as discriminability saturation (distribution deformation), not test-loss collapse"
    cited: false

  - id: kazdan2025collapse
    title: "Collapse or Thrive? Perils and Promises of Synthetic Data in a Self-Generating World"
    authors: "Kazdan, Schaeffer et al."
    venue: "ICML 2025"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.16713"
    category: "model-collapse"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Accumulate vs replace regimes affect contamination dynamics; in accumulate regime K* may shift upward"
    cited: false

  - id: he2025generalization
    title: "A Closer Look at Model Collapse: From a Generalization-to-Memorization Perspective"
    authors: "He et al."
    venue: "NeurIPS 2025"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.16499"
    code: "https://shilianghe007.github.io/model-collapse/"
    category: "model-collapse"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Generalization-to-memorization transition in iterative retraining parallels our feature-space convergence; entropy decrease over iterations aligns with our depth-discriminative features"
    cited: false

  # === Should-Cite ===

  - id: basani2026diveye
    title: "DivEye: Diversity Boosts AI-Generated Text Detection"
    authors: "Basani, Chen"
    venue: "TMLR 2026"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18880"
    code: "https://github.com/IBM/diveye"
    category: "detection"
    role: "method-component"
    relevance: "Surprisal diversity features as potential baseline for depth estimation; zero-shot detector outperforms prior work by 33.2%"
    cited: false

  - id: amin2025escaping
    title: "Escaping Collapse: The Strength of Weak Data for Large Language Model Training"
    authors: "Amin et al."
    venue: "NeurIPS 2025"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08924"
    category: "verification-curation"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Boosting-inspired framework showing weak signal suffices for iterative training; motivates practical utility of imperfect depth estimators"
    cited: false

  - id: zawalski2026codec
    title: "CoDeC: Detecting Data Contamination in LLMs via In-Context Learning"
    authors: "Zawalski et al."
    venue: "ICLR 2026"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.27055"
    category: "contamination"
    role: "evaluation"
    relevance: "Binary contamination detection via ICL confidence shifts; complementary to our finer-grained depth estimation approach"
    cited: false

  - id: gambetta2025surplexity
    title: "Learning by Surprise: Surplexity for Mitigating Model Collapse"
    authors: "Gambetta et al."
    venue: "arXiv preprint 2025"
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12341"
    category: "verification-curation"
    role: "evaluation"
    relevance: "Surprise-based collapse metric; surplexity scores as potential feature for depth estimation pipeline and baseline comparison"
    cited: false
